test_title: PYST 71: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Urea Subsidy Scheme:

Statement 1: Urea is sold to farmers at a fixed Maximum Retail Price (MRP).

Statement 2: The subsidy is directly transferred to the bank accounts of farmers.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urea** is the only fertilizer in India that remains under statutory price control. The **Government of India** fixes a uniform **Maximum Retail Price (MRP)** for urea across the country, ensuring it remains affordable for the farming community. The current MRP is approximately **Rs 242 per 45 kg bag** (excluding taxes and neem coating charges). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Under the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** system for fertilizers, the subsidy is not paid directly to the farmers' bank accounts. Instead, the **Government of India** pays the subsidy amount directly to the **fertilizer companies** (manufacturers or importers) after the actual sale is made to the farmer through a **Point of Sale (PoS)** device. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Urea Subsidy** is the difference between the **cost of production** (for domestic units) or the **Import Parity Price (IPP)** (for imported urea) and the fixed **MRP** paid by the farmers. This entire fiscal burden is borne by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neem Coated Urea (NCU):**

 
 
• In **2015**, the government made it mandatory for all domestic producers to produce **100% Neem Coated Urea**.
 
• This initiative was launched to prevent the **illegal diversion** of highly subsidized urea for industrial uses and to improve **Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE)**.
 
 
 
• **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme:**
 
 
• Unlike urea, Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilizers like **DAP** and **MOP** are governed by the **NBS Scheme** launched in **April 2010**.
 
• Under **NBS**, a fixed amount of subsidy is provided based on the nutrient content (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potash, and Sulphur) rather than a fixed retail price.
 
 
 
• **New Urea Policy (NUP) 2015:**
 
 
• The **NUP 2015** was implemented to maximize indigenous production, promote **energy efficiency** in urea plants, and rationalize the total subsidy burden.
